TOP NEWS " Cracks emerge in Texas' economy as job growth slows" ($) " Colleagues recall that he spent 41 years practicing journalism 'the right way'" ($) 2025 " The Silence of the Shams" 2026 " How Ken Paxton, a Rising MAGA Star, Got Rich as a Texas Politician," Wall Street Journal's Elizabeth Findley and Mark Maremont \-- "Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton went from being a middle-class lawyer to a multimillionaire during his two decades on a public official's salary, according to thousands of pages of previously unreported documents that shed new light on the personal finances of one of the Republican Party's most-watched midterm candidates. Paxton, who entered state government in 2003 with a modest income and few assets, by 2018 told a lender he had amassed a net worth of about $5.5 million, not including millions in assets he and his wife had previously moved into a blind trust. The following year, Paxton reaped an additional $2.2 million gain--never previously disclosed--from his investment in a local company with a lucrative Texas state contract, according to the documents reviewed by The Wall Street Journal, which include Paxton's tax returns and bank statements. Paxton's accumulation of wealth has become a key campaign issue as he vies to unseat U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in set for March 3, 2026. The race is crucial to Republicans' hopes to hold on to their Senate majority. Paxton is popular with the party's base, but national GOP strategists fear his nomination could cost them in a general election. Cornyn has cast suspicion on Paxton's finances and highlighted the attorney general's failures to fully disclose them. Paxton has sought to paint Cornyn as a Washington insider. U.S. Rep. Wesley Hunt said Monday he is joining the Republican primary field as well. Paxton, 62 years old, became a rising star in the MAGA world, winning support for his battles on issues such as abortion, border security and efforts to overturn the 2020 election. But allegations of corruption and other impropriety have surfaced repeatedly during Paxton's career. The Republican-majority Texas House voted to impeach him in 2023 over allegations that he abused his office to aid a campaign donor, which he denied. The Texas Senate acquitted and returned him to office after a two-week trial. A spokesman for Paxton called this article a "bogus hit piece" given to The Wall Street Journal by Paxton's political enemies. The documents reviewed by the Journal were produced via subpoena by banks and other parties for the impeachment trial. Most were never entered into evidence and haven't been previously disclosed. The documents include seven years of Paxton's tax returns; personal financial statements prepared by Paxton and his wife for a series of property loans; personal bank records; the bank records of his blind trust; and text messages between Paxton, his wife and the trustee of the blind trust. Angela Paxton , a Texas state senator, filed for divorce from Paxton in July, citing adultery as the reason for ending 38 years of marriage. Angela Paxton declined to comment, via a spokesman. Paxton in 2015 put his assets into a blind trust, a tool used by politicians to avoid conflicts of interest by separating them from management of their money. Although he said in public filings that he would no longer know what assets were in his trust, the text messages show a closer involvement, including in one instance his trustee texting Paxton updates on stock trades. Making a fortune Before Paxton first ran for public office in 2002, his only listed assets were a handful of stocks and a house with a mortgage, with a combined value of less than $175,000, according to an analysis of his 2001 state financial-disclosure form. At the time, he was an attorney and his wife, a former public-school teacher, was homeschooling their four children. Both came from modest upbringings. Over the next dozen years, as Paxton was re-elected to the state House and then the Texas Senate, he disclosed owning interests in more partnerships and private companies in annual ethics filings. It is unclear from the filings where the money came from to buy them or how much they were worth. Texas' annual ethics filings don't require public officials to disclose their total income, net worth or the value of holdings in business entities. Paxton previously has taken the position that assets within the blind trust don't need to be disclosed. Paxton provided more information to his banks, the documents show. In 2015, his first year as attorney general, a personal financial statement he provided to a bank pegged the couple's total net worth at $5.4 million, roughly 40% of it from investments that they had moved into the blind trust earlier that year. On that year's tax return, he and his wife reported earning a combined $161,000 from their salaries as a state employee and a Christian school guidance counselor. They reported about $200,000 in additional income, mostly from investments. A $2.2 million windfall arrived in 2019. The gain derived from Paxton's 2004 investment in a police video technology company, later named WatchGuard, that he had shifted into the blind trust. Paxton, who reported investing about $300,000 in WatchGuard, cashed out with a huge gain when the company was bought by in 2019 for about $250 million. The investment had drawn scrutiny over the years in Texas, sparked by ethics concerns about a lucrative contract the company obtained in 2006 from the Texas Department of Public Safety while Paxton was an investor and a state legislator. Paxton said in 2008 that he wasn't aware the company had a state contract. Two years after the big gain, the Paxtons and their blind trust went on a 10-month , spending almost $3.5 million on residential properties in Florida, Oklahoma, Utah and Hawaii. They took out mortgages to pay for some of the properties. Last year Paxton bought an $800,000 condo, at a resort in Ivins, Utah, and transferred it into the trust in March 2025, according to public records. The Paxtons now own at least 11 residential properties around the U.S. with an assessed value of $7.5 million. Blind trust The blind trust the Paxtons voluntarily established in 2015, called the Esther Blind Trust, is structured to block the couple from knowledge of their investments. Its governing documents say that the trustee must act without providing them information other than what is narrowly required for trust maintenance. Paxton publicly affirmed he had no knowledge of trust investments in his 2015 state ethics filing. He told one of his banks that neither he nor his wife "have knowledge of the current investments." But the text messages with the trust's trustee, Charles Loper III , show otherwise. In March 2020, Loper texted Ken Paxton a list of eight stock buys worth a combined $618,000. The trust's bank-account records show it had made the buys the day before. Legal experts called the texting of the stock trades a potential violation of ethics statutes defining blind trusts as blind only if the trust is managed without consultation. "That would be an occasion in which a blind trust is blind in name only," Texas trust attorneyBrad Wiewel said. Loper didn't respond to requests for comment. In the summer of 2020, Angela Paxton texted Loper: "Please keep me informed of any financial actions initiated by Ken and don't assume I am aware even if he tells you I consent." Loper is a close friend of the Paxtons from church who had gifted Ken Paxton $20,000 for his legal defense. Texas law requires a trustee to be a "disinterested party."" **Will ‘junk science’ law secure Roberson a new trial?**

“He is actually innocent,”**Gretchen Sween** , one of Roberson’s attorneys, told reporters after the court ruling. “I would like to prove that and get him home one day.”

Roberson’s attorneys have argued his then-undiagnosed autism helped convict him as authorities and medical personnel felt he didn’t act like a concerned parent because his flat affect was seen as a sign of guilt. He was diagnosed with autism in 2018.

Roberson’s lawyers argue that the two cases are indistinguishable.

The appeals court sent Roberson’s case back to his trial court in East Texas for review to determine if he should get a new trial.

**Matthew Bowman** , Nikki’s half-brother, said he and his family are disappointed by Thursday’s ruling, and that they think Roberson should be executed. Bowman told The Associated Press he believes the evidence shows Roberson caused Nikki’s injuries by repeatedly hitting her.

“In my opinion, he’s the only one that could have done it that night. So we’re hoping that the execution comes back,” he said.

The Texas Attorney General’s Office, which is seeking Roberson’s execution, has not responded to an email requesting comment.

**Appeals court focuses on similar shaken baby syndrome case**

Roberson’s lawyers had requested the stay based new legal and scientific developments and expert analyses that indicate Nikki’s death was caused by illness and accident, not abuse. They included a joint statement from 10 independent pathologists who said the medical examiner’s autopsy report, which concluded Nikki died from blunt force head injuries, was “not reliable.”

Roberson’s attorneys also alleged judicial misconduct, saying the judge who oversaw his trial hadn’t disclosed he previously authorized the circumvention of Roberson’s parental rights and allowed Nikki’s grandparents to remove her from life support.

The appeals court denied both those claims and instead said it was granting the stay to review issues raised by Roark’s case on its “own initiative.”

In granting Roark a new trial, the appeals court found that the science had changed to undermine the prosecution’s theory of a case involving shaken baby syndrome, and that Roark likely would not have been convicted under the “evolved scientific evidence.” The Dallas County District Attorney’s Office subsequently dropped the charges against Roark.

“I know that Roark changed the legal landscape in Texas and should mean relief for Robert,” Sween said.

**“How Ken Paxton, a Rising MAGA Star, Got Rich as a Texas Politician,”** Wall Street Journal’s **Elizabeth Findley and Mark Maremont** \-- “Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** went from being a middle-class lawyer to a multimillionaire during his two decades on a public official’s salary, according to thousands of pages of previously unreported documents that shed new light on the personal finances of one of the Republican Party’s most-watched midterm candidates.

Paxton, who entered state government in 2003 with a modest income and few assets, by 2018 told a lender he had amassed a net worth of about $5.5 million, not including millions in assets he and his wife had previously moved into a blind trust.

The following year, Paxton reaped an additional $2.2 million gain—never previously disclosed—from his investment in a local company with a lucrative Texas state contract, according to the documents reviewed by The Wall Street Journal, which include Paxton’s tax returns and bank statements.

Paxton’s accumulation of wealth has become a key campaign issue as he vies to unseat U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** in [a hotly contested Republican primary](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eGUT-qZUuq6VAj7Pk0pzqLTd0DhGcCOlLXX7wtpM_Vdt8o2CfZId1piqyJmylXsKI0LWXxh-7xxJr6b1AT4vM1TZuLudA--MND02EzE1xTQEUfTdtMAfzrjlw09W5CeYvCv7uWxpLTKdukxZcgH2Gz-ePhItMQn3gyIqLoem_GFfiJaVlT2i-v2bnqG0zBeiXysodBlVOGwifBygrx804Np9hqHrrM9caB8Ucny8unE-hAtd86EgCdz0S8G8E-S-UrAT22JZPgY_wOF28btfnzWUXXK7a-hr367O5EJTXsiiLo9aqB-Jsw-y2IzZqE72NNDAIu-Xgb5N6qidFOUkLvgRM4I4wsKe2BmubonHhb059h8s4L50jkV_vsR3xyONXD9Ngwza9xEnpDibOcLf2X8dNA7iPoPiNRMU9ldAmsna1QUjzWsleahFGkPDh_FcBzV-fiqH2G7bS1yaYnujEDaTc7pBcuInvDVBqxgGH2LfQvShHenc-LtZmOccxvyLhg/4km/SVmjjpDmQJCjb-Rb37C2fw/h36/h001.m3KyHLqbVIN4KAwYOmg9QRaV91jCgNJOzBQoIsTVs4A) set for March 3, 2026. The race is crucial to Republicans’ hopes to hold on to their Senate majority. Paxton is popular with the party’s base, but national GOP strategists fear his nomination could cost them in a general election.

Cornyn has cast suspicion on Paxton’s finances and highlighted the attorney general’s failures to fully disclose them. Paxton has sought to paint Cornyn as a Washington insider. U.S. Rep. **Wesley Hunt** said Monday he is joining the Republican primary field as well.

Paxton, 62 years old, became a rising star in the MAGA world, winning support for his battles on issues such as abortion, border security and efforts to overturn the 2020 election.

But allegations of corruption and other impropriety have surfaced repeatedly during Paxton’s career. The Republican-majority Texas House voted to impeach him in 2023 over allegations that he abused his office to aid a campaign donor, which he denied. The Texas Senate acquitted and returned him to office after a two-week trial.

A spokesman for Paxton called this article a “bogus hit piece” given to The Wall Street Journal by Paxton’s political enemies.

The documents reviewed by the Journal were produced via subpoena by banks and other parties for the impeachment trial. Most were never entered into evidence and haven’t been previously disclosed. The documents include seven years of Paxton’s tax returns; personal financial statements prepared by Paxton and his wife for a series of property loans; personal bank records; the bank records of his blind trust; and text messages between Paxton, his wife and the trustee of the blind trust.

**Angela Paxton** , a Texas state senator, filed for divorce from Paxton in July, citing adultery as the reason for ending 38 years of marriage.

Angela Paxton declined to comment, via a spokesman.

Paxton in 2015 put his assets into a blind trust, a tool used by politicians to avoid conflicts of interest by separating them from management of their money. Although he said in public filings that he would no longer know what assets were in his trust, the text messages show a closer involvement, including in one instance his trustee texting Paxton updates on stock trades.

**Making a fortune**

Before Paxton first ran for public office in 2002, his only listed assets were a handful of stocks and a house with a mortgage, with a combined value of less than $175,000, according to an analysis of his 2001 state financial-disclosure form. At the time, he was an attorney and his wife, a former public-school teacher, was homeschooling their four children. Both came from modest upbringings.

Over the next dozen years, as Paxton was re-elected to the state House and then the Texas Senate, he disclosed owning interests in more partnerships and private companies in annual ethics filings. It is unclear from the filings where the money came from to buy them or how much they were worth.

Texas’ annual ethics filings don’t require public officials to disclose their total income, net worth or the value of holdings in business entities. Paxton previously has taken the position that assets within the blind trust don’t need to be disclosed.

Paxton provided more information to his banks, the documents show. In 2015, his first year as attorney general, a personal financial statement he provided to a bank pegged the couple’s total net worth at $5.4 million, roughly 40% of it from investments that they had moved into the blind trust earlier that year.

On that year’s tax return, he and his wife reported earning a combined $161,000 from their salaries as a state employee and a Christian school guidance counselor. They reported about $200,000 in additional income, mostly from investments.

A $2.2 million windfall arrived in 2019. The gain derived from Paxton’s 2004 investment in a police video technology company, later named WatchGuard, that he had shifted into the blind trust. Paxton, who reported investing about $300,000 in WatchGuard, cashed out with a huge gain when the company was bought by [Motorola Solutions](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eAbNCulTSOsog31_JqTApIpOWMgQm2gDiLv2TNqMj9BuOtU66MU90uV2G1bqus63CdR1DwFsRP9U-YNujc2wGMAjpUPHuOTyvcb5ZGZrr5IrQShWaK2ovWIL6NYXxkH1fDAUi66sAOWfPlbUPApf53dRqIfQ8oONMn-Cs4Qrf44tMYyE-o-cCvT43B7tQ89pESIBb65tXYIDADjvsnp5Vv25MydDHL5X8IO2vQsvEaClOfH-4TDIa4DPzsQRKKFqWO4KN0PEwYtU4RdVx18xcOvI4PM5O4wfLtFPoI9beDka7mggfky9OCad995nEyg2K4LPimMriUoQveSfX11RtlSWeCrguDZA1Sm0K_YcfbtKbr7JGpsDUuZC7AKZDd6HXirrZXyxTYIEliDbLkoALLN1d6wjBycLSreDmwGVXRqE/4km/SVmjjpDmQJCjb-Rb37C2fw/h37/h001.b33hDpLjSlzo2Br4LGbSNyfVGrEbM0U_D_GpQX9Tab8) in 2019 for about $250 million.

**Blind trust**

The blind trust the Paxtons voluntarily established in 2015, called the Esther Blind Trust, is structured to block the couple from knowledge of their investments. Its governing documents say that the trustee must act without providing them information other than what is narrowly required for trust maintenance.

Paxton publicly affirmed he had no knowledge of trust investments in his 2015 state ethics filing. He told one of his banks that neither he nor his wife “have knowledge of the current investments.”

But the text messages with the trust’s trustee, **Charles Loper III** , show otherwise.

In March 2020, Loper texted Ken Paxton a list of eight stock buys worth a combined $618,000. The trust’s bank-account records show it had made the buys the day before.

Legal experts called the texting of the stock trades a potential violation of ethics statutes defining blind trusts as blind only if the trust is managed without consultation.

“That would be an occasion in which a blind trust is blind in name only,” Texas trust attorney**Brad Wiewel** said.

Loper didn’t respond to requests for comment.

In the summer of 2020, Angela Paxton texted Loper: “Please keep me informed of any financial actions initiated by Ken and don’t assume I am aware even if he tells you I consent.”

Roberson had been scheduled to receive a lethal injection for the death of his 2-year-old daughter Nikki Curtis. » Since his first execution date more than nine years ago, Roberson’s lawyers have filed multiple petitions with state and federal appeals courts, as well as with the U.S. Supreme Court, to stop his execution. They have also asked the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles and Gov. Greg Abbott to intervene, as part of their efforts to secure Roberson a new trial. He was diagnosed with autism in 2018. The court granted the stay based on Texas’ 2013 , which allows a person convicted of a crime to seek relief if the evidence used against them is no longer credible. It cited its October 2024 ruling that overturned the conviction of another man, Andrew Roark , in another shaken baby case in Dallas. Roberson’s lawyers argue that the two cases are indistinguishable. The appeals court sent Roberson’s case back to his trial court in East Texas for review to determine if he should get a new trial. Matthew Bowman , Nikki’s half-brother, said he and his family are disappointed by Thursday’s ruling, and that they think Roberson should be executed. Bowman told The Associated Press he believes the evidence shows Roberson caused Nikki’s injuries by repeatedly hitting her. “In my opinion, he’s the only one that could have done it that night. Appeals court focuses on similar shaken baby syndrome case Roberson’s lawyers had requested the stay based new legal and scientific developments and expert analyses that indicate Nikki’s death was caused by illness and accident, not abuse. They included a joint statement from 10 independent pathologists who said the medical examiner’s autopsy report, which concluded Nikki died from blunt force head injuries, was “not reliable.” Roberson’s attorneys also alleged judicial misconduct, saying the judge who oversaw his trial hadn’t disclosed he previously authorized the circumvention of Roberson’s parental rights and allowed Nikki’s grandparents to remove her from life support. The appeals court denied both those claims and instead said it was granting the stay to review issues raised by Roark’s case on its “own initiative.” In granting Roark a new trial, the appeals court found that the science had changed to undermine the prosecution’s theory of a case involving shaken baby syndrome, and that Roark likely would not have been convicted under the “evolved scientific evidence.” The Dallas County District Attorney’s Office subsequently dropped the charges against Roark. “I know that Roark changed the legal landscape in Texas and should mean relief for Robert,” Sween said. The diagnosis of shaken baby syndrome refers to a serious brain injury caused when a child’s head is hurt through shaking or some other violent impact, like being slammed against a wall or thrown on the floor. Prosecutors and say it remains valid. Roberson’s supporters include , Texas GOP megadonor and conservative activist Doug Deason , bestselling author John Grisham , and Brian Wharton , the former police detective who helped put together the case against him. GOP state Rep. Paxton, who entered state government in 2003 with a modest income and few assets, by 2018 told a lender he had amassed a net worth of about $5.5 million, not including millions in assets he and his wife had previously moved into a blind trust. The following year, Paxton reaped an additional $2.2 million gain—never previously disclosed—from his investment in a local company with a lucrative Texas state contract, according to the documents reviewed by The Wall Street Journal, which include Paxton’s tax returns and bank statements. Paxton’s accumulation of wealth has become a key campaign issue as he vies to unseat U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in set for March 3, 2026. The race is crucial to Republicans’ hopes to hold on to their Senate majority. Paxton is popular with the party’s base, but national GOP strategists fear his nomination could cost them in a general election. Paxton, 62 years old, became a rising star in the MAGA world, winning support for his battles on issues such as abortion, border security and efforts to overturn the 2020 election. But allegations of corruption and other impropriety have surfaced repeatedly during Paxton’s career. The Republican-majority Texas House voted to impeach him in 2023 over allegations that he abused his office to aid a campaign donor, which he denied. The Texas Senate acquitted and returned him to office after a two-week trial. A spokesman for Paxton called this article a “bogus hit piece” given to The Wall Street Journal by Paxton’s political enemies. The documents reviewed by the Journal were produced via subpoena by banks and other parties for the impeachment trial. Most were never entered into evidence and haven’t been previously disclosed. The documents include seven years of Paxton’s tax returns; personal financial statements prepared by Paxton and his wife for a series of property loans; personal bank records; the bank records of his blind trust; and text messages between Paxton, his wife and the trustee of the blind trust. Angela Paxton , a Texas state senator, filed for divorce from Paxton in July, citing adultery as the reason for ending 38 years of marriage. Angela Paxton declined to comment, via a spokesman. Paxton in 2015 put his assets into a blind trust, a tool used by politicians to avoid conflicts of interest by separating them from management of their money. Making a fortune Before Paxton first ran for public office in 2002, his only listed assets were a handful of stocks and a house with a mortgage, with a combined value of less than $175,000, according to an analysis of his 2001 state financial-disclosure form. Texas’ annual ethics filings don’t require public officials to disclose their total income, net worth or the value of holdings in business entities. Paxton previously has taken the position that assets within the blind trust don’t need to be disclosed. Paxton provided more information to his banks, the documents show. In 2015, his first year as attorney general, a personal financial statement he provided to a bank pegged the couple’s total net worth at $5.4 million, roughly 40% of it from investments that they had moved into the blind trust earlier that year. On that year’s tax return, he and his wife reported earning a combined $161,000 from their salaries as a state employee and a Christian school guidance counselor. They reported about $200,000 in additional income, mostly from investments. A $2.2 million windfall arrived in 2019. Paxton, who reported investing about $300,000 in WatchGuard, cashed out with a huge gain when the company was bought by in 2019 for about $250 million. Last year Paxton bought an $800,000 condo, at a resort in Ivins, Utah, and transferred it into the trust in March 2025, according to public records. Its governing documents say that the trustee must act without providing them information other than what is narrowly required for trust maintenance. Loper didn’t respond to requests for comment. In the summer of 2020, Angela Paxton texted Loper: “Please keep me informed of any financial actions initiated by Ken and don’t assume I am aware even if he tells you I consent.” Loper is a close friend of the Paxtons from church who had gifted Ken Paxton $20,000 for his legal defense. name: Gabby Giffords
subject: It’s been one month

body:
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q42025.UDsFRy&refcode=em250912-1-b&t=1&akid=10950%2E3935704%2Ej6_5ZC)
---
Team, it’s Gabby Giffords.
Today marks exactly one month since the assassination of Charlie Kirk. After the shooting, I wrote an op-ed for TIME Magazine discussing the rise of politically motivated attacks and the need to keep our communities safe from gun violence.
We may never be able to eliminate all gun violence—but we must realize that all gun violence is preventable. But it’s on all of us to step up.
I’ve attached the op-ed below. Thank you for reading.
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q42025.UDsFRy&refcode=em250912-1-b&t=2&akid=10950%2E3935704%2Ej6_5ZC)**

* * *
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q42025.UDsFRy&refcode=em250912-1-b&t=3&akid=10950%2E3935704%2Ej6_5ZC)
I mourn for Charlie Kirk’s family.
I didn’t agree with almost anything he said, but he had a right to speak. Just as he had a right to go on a work trip and return safely to his wife and two young children at home in the state we share, Arizona.
Just as Melissa Hortman, the Speaker of the Minnesota State Legislature, deserved to be safe at home with her husband and her dog. Instead they were all three shot dead together one night in June.
Just as President Donald Trump had the right to campaign without fear of being assassinated, as two different people tried to do last summer.
Just as I had the right to meet with my constituents safely on January 8, 2011 — the day when instead I, a young congresswoman in a purple district, was nearly assassinated. Eighteen other people were shot and six were killed.
Our stories are unique, but what Charlie Kirk, President Trump, Melissa Hortman and I all have in common is that someone who wanted to kill us had a gun.
We can and should talk about political violence, and its toxic relationship to political rhetoric. We can and must talk about social media’s role in these moments. We all, as individual Americans, need to do a better job considering our words and their impact. But anyone who responds to preventable tragedies like this—tragedies that over time begin to erode the very fabric of our country—by refusing to face the problem of gun violence and crime head-on is missing the point.
What we share, and what puts all of us in danger—from elected leaders to little children, like those shot while praying in church in Minnesota a few weeks ago—is the overwhelming prevalence of guns in this country and the loopholes that make it appallingly easy for dangerous people to access them.
In America, we now have more guns than people. Many states take sensible steps—background checks, extreme risk protection orders, and safe storage laws—all policies that help reduce gun crime and gun deaths. Other states—like Utah, which year after year receives a F grade in the annual Gun Law Scorecard released by my organization, GIFFORDS—do far too little to save lives. Utah has expanded gun access in recent years, and gun deaths have increased along with that, soaring by 45% from 2014 to 2023, according to the CDC.
I was gutted to learn that Charlie Kirk died yesterday in Utah—and it’s also true that in Utah, someone dies from gun violence every 20 hours. Too many families know the pain of having a loved one killed by guns, in that state and across the country.
In fact, mere hours after Kirk’s shooting, at least two students were shot at a high school in Evergreen, Colorado.
Americans of both political parties desperately want this violence to end. Our research suggests that the vast majority of Republican voters want to close loopholes that allow criminals and dangerous people to get their hands on guns. When you ask parents what they want most for their children’s education, they tell us again and again that keeping their kids safe from gun violence is their top priority. The American people are far more united than their representatives in Washington. Our polling shows 88% of Republicans support background checks on all gun sales, 75% support laws to get untraceable ghost guns off the streets, and a surprising 81% support requiring a license to own a gun (just like Americans need licenses to drive cars). Yet somehow Congress refuses to act.
It is physically very hard for me to speak due to my injuries from the bullets that hit me that day in January, and after watching yet another political shooting violently steal someone’s life before our eyes, it’s even harder to find words. So I want to speak plainly to my former colleagues in Congress, both the House and the Senate: Do something. Take action. Pray also if you want, but understand: your job is action. Nobody goes to the polls to elect someone to pray for them. We vote because we trust the people we elect will pass sensible, moderate policies that make our country a better, safer place to live and raise a family.
We may never be able to eliminate all gun violence. But we must realize that all gun violence is preventable. We know what to do to make our country safer for all of us, and our elected representatives can do it immediately. Come to the table, as Republicans and Democrats, to pass solutions to the epidemic of gun violence that’s killing both of us. There’s no shortage of policies with a history of bipartisan support: closing background check loopholes, supporting violence intervention programs, funding law enforcement—including the brave agents at the ATF who catch violent criminals and crack down on the small percentage of gun dealers who break the law—among many others. Above all: prioritize American lives over the donations and profits of gun industry CEOs.
When I was shot, my friend Judge John Roll was killed. He was a Republican. We didn’t always agree, but we still worked together for the good of our state. Also killed was Christina-Taylor Green. She was only nine years old and had just been elected Class President at her elementary school. Their families will never be whole again, just as the Kirk family will never be whole again, and I hold them all in my heart.
I call on my colleagues in Washington to show courage, not cowardice. I call on them to show loyalty to our country and our common values, and to do the single most important thing they can for their constituents: keep them safe.
* * *

Please, take a second to read this...
As a victim of political violence, Gabby Giffords has led the fight to save more lives from gun violence for more than a decade, but she can’t do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to pass commonsense gun safety legislation across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
**If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to contribute to GIFFORDS PAC today.**

Come to the table, as Republicans and Democrats, to pass solutions to the epidemic of gun violence that’s killing both of us. There’s no shortage of policies with a history of bipartisan support: closing background check loopholes, supporting violence intervention programs, funding law enforcement—including the brave agents at the ATF who catch violent criminals and crack down on the small percentage of gun dealers who break the law—among many others. Above all: prioritize American lives over the donations and profits of gun industry CEOs. When I was shot, my friend Judge John Roll was killed. He was a Republican. We didn’t always agree, but we still worked together for the good of our state. Also killed was Christina-Taylor Green. She was only nine years old and had just been elected Class President at her elementary school. Their families will never be whole again, just as the Kirk family will never be whole again, and I hold them all in my heart. I call on my colleagues in Washington to show courage, not cowardice. I call on them to show loyalty to our country and our common values, and to do the single most important thing they can for their constituents: keep them safe. Please, take a second to read this... As a victim of political violence, Gabby Giffords has led the fight to save more lives from gun violence for more than a decade, but she can’t do it alone. If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to pass commonsense gun safety legislation across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can. If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to contribute to GIFFORDS PAC today. We need 7,500 combined volunteer hours to help us get back on track and reach our phone call goal.

As you read this message, California voters are returning their mail ballot for Proposition 50.
We have ambitious voter outreach goals in the final weeks of this election. Talking to voters directly on why they should vote YES and to return their ballot as soon as possible. The truth is we need more volunteers in and out of California to step up.
This election doesn’t just impact California, it impacts us nationally. Just look at the volunteer activity since last month. Every blue dot represents a volunteer taking action to stand up against Trump from stealing the election next year.
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/5149?t=1&akid=2663%2E4767699%2EF97rZo)
We’re exceeding our goals on texting, knocking on doors, and talking to friends and family, but **we’re behind on our phone calls to voters. 7,500 combined volunteer hours will help us get back on track and reach our goal by November 4.**
That’s 7,500 volunteers putting in one hour of their time to call voters. Our campaign makes it incredibly simple to participate, using our call tool and virtual access through Zoom. You can make calls from anywhere with just a computer, laptop, or tablet and a smartphone.
**[Can you join a virtual phone bank? Find a date and time that works for you. When you sign up, you’ll receive a Zoom link to join the virtual phone bank.](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/5149?t=2&akid=2663%2E4767699%2EF97rZo)**

Everyone who has already stepped up is hoping you’ll join them in this campaign, and we hope to see you make up a new dot on our volunteer map.
Thank you,
Team Newsom

# Trump declares Oct 13 is Columbus Day! "We're back Italians!"
President Donald Trump opened Thursday's Cabinet meeting by signing proclamations to observe both Leif Erikson Day (October 9) honoring the Viking explorer who discovered Newfoundland 1,000 years ago, **[and Columbus Day](https://substack.com/redirect/c3319753-757f-40d1-9ba8-e3f7d297bf7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** celebrating Christopher Columbus's 1492 voyage to the New World.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9a1ee613-a114-439a-940a-6fbbce652a59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **" We're back, Italians!" declaration**: Trump received applause for the Columbus Day proclamation and declared "We're back, Italians!" as he emphasized his commitment to restoring Columbus Day to prominence after progressives attempted to tarnish Columbus's achievement and legacy.
* **Reversal of Democratic policies** : Trump previously announced in April he was "bringing Columbus Day back from the ashes," criticizing Democrats for trying "to destroy Christopher Columbus" by tearing down statues and replacing the holiday with "WOKE" alternatives, vowing to reinstate Columbus Day "under the same rules, dates, and locations" as before.

# Nobel committee awards this year's peace prize, and it wasn't to Trump...
The Norwegian Nobel Committee **[awarded this year's peace prize to Maria Corina Machado](https://substack.com/redirect/60bbc13b-de4f-4fb0-a874-9f2099655859?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, a Venezuelan opposition leader recognized for her "tireless work promoting democratic rights" and struggle to achieve a peaceful transition from dictatorship to democracy in Venezuela.
* **Trump supporters disappointed, cite peace achievements** : White House Communications Director Steven Cheung criticized the committee for placing "politics over peace," arguing Trump "will continue making peace deals, ending wars, and saving lives," though Trump missed this year's January 31 nomination deadline and could be eligible for 2026.
* **Israeli hostage families advocate for Trump** : The Hostages and Missing Families Forum wrote to the Nobel Committee stating "no leader or organization has contributed more to peace around the world than President Trump," emphasizing he has "delivered tangible results that have saved countless lives" rather than offering "empty promises."
* **Netanyahu formally nominated Trump** : Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Trump in July that he nominated him for the Nobel Peace Prize, citing the Abraham Accords and Trump's role in "forging peace...in one country and one region after the other," presenting Trump with the nomination letter during a Washington D.C. meeting.

name: Marialana Kinter
subject: Personal Invitation - CONCERT Kinter For Congress
body:
Good afternoon,

I'm writing to you today to extend a personal invitation to a very exciting event we have coming up.
**On Saturday, November 1st at 7PM, our campaign is holding an exclusive fundraising concert with Nashville country artist Trey Taylor!**
Trey's team reached out to us directly because he was inspired by our campaign's mission. Trey's story is incredible: he is the youngest African-American artist ever signed to a Nashville country music deal, and inspired by his own philanthropic drive, he has made it his mission to support leaders who are fighting for justice and unity.

He sees our race as a place where "moral clarity and community-first leadership can make a national impact," and he's generously offering his talent to help us win.
To protect the integrity of the show and for safety, we are not advertising this event on social media. Instead, I am personally extending this invitation to you directly. Please feel free to share this with friends, family, and anyone you know who would be inspired by this special night.
Tickets are available at tiered levels, and we are also looking for supporters to join our host committee for the event.
** _To make it even more exciting, the first 50 people who purchase tickets will receive a_**** _personalized video invitation from Trey himself_!**
This is a powerful opportunity to show the strength of our grassroots movement. I would be honored if you would join us.
**You can get your tickets and learn more here:** <https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trey4marialana>
Thank you for being in this fight with me.
In solidarity

\--

Marialana Kinter
_U.S. Navy Veteran | Congressional Candidate, FL-07
_
‪321.247.8403‬
[KinterForCongress.com](http://KinterForCongress.com)

Trump declared this so-called emergency on the first day of his presidency, letting the administration block clean energy projects, fast-track the approvals of fossil fuel projects, and bypass bedrock environmental laws.
Why? To please his donors!
Billionaires and Big Oil don’t need handouts from the President — especially at the expense of everyday Americans’ energy bills!
Thanks to my GOP colleagues blocking this legislation, we’ll continue to see energy prices go up, good clean energy projects canceled, and good-paying manufacturing jobs lost. When our bills go up, we’ll all know who to blame.
It’s time for my Republican colleagues to take the side of the American people over Trump’s donors.

Hello,
In a moment, I'm going to ask you to make a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts here in Nebraska. But before I do, please let me explain why your donation today is so important.
I'm not rich. I'm not a politician. I'm a blue collar guy who was president of my local union until I was fired for leading a strike.
People like me aren't supposed to be able to run for office – let alone U.S. Senate – and we certainly aren't supposed to be able to win...
**But last year we did almost just that. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country. And now, I'm running again for the U.S. Senate – this time against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts.**
In the Senate, I'll be the 51st vote to protect our democracy, the 51st vote to stop the corruption and get money out of politics, and the 51st vote to stand up against the billionaires like Ricketts who have been screwing over working people like me for decades.
And that's exactly why the Super PACs are going to come after me twice as hard this time to try to stop us again from flipping this seat.
**We need to raise $50,000 before our fundraising deadline if we're going to be able to fight back against the lies and win this Senate seat – but right now, we're still short with time running out.**
**[I have nowhere else to turn: Please, will you split a donation right now between my campaign and Jacky Rosen's to help me defeat billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts and flip Nebraska's Senate seat?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117007245/575109165/358649031?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5619-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMGE4MDg3Zi1lYWE1LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=v_5A5JI2q6sFwvbvsw6zf8gYd09e3GioXdAUhtkVSFE=)**
I know what it's like to work a 90-hour workweek. I know the value of a dollar. So I truly appreciate any amount you can afford to give.
Thank you – from the bottom of my heart,

Dan Osborn

| Peter,
The very fate of our Democracy and the electoral future of the Democratic party rests upon a Democratic victory in the sleepy and often overlooked 2025 Pennsylvania Supreme Court Retention Election.
If we lose this court, MAGA will seize control of Pennsylvania and will implement an extreme abortion ban, redistrict the PA congressional map making it blood red, and rig the '26 midterms and '28 presidential in the penultimate swing state - 19 electoral college votes down the drain.
Republicans pulled off a shocking lightning breakthrough last month and early polling now shows that a catastrophic loss is exactly what Democrats are on track for. These three factors explain why the GOP is winning:

1. Voter registration \- over the Summer, the Pennsylvania GOP shrunk the million voter registration gap that Democrats once held over Republicans to just a 50,000 vote lead. If these trends continue they will surpass Democrats before our November 4th Election Day.

2. Spending \- bankrolled by the likes of Jeff Yass, the richest man in Pennsylvania, Elon Musk, and Tristan Tate, accused human trafficker and brother of masculinity influencer Andrew Tate, the GOP effort to seize this court boasts a 10-1 spending advantage over Democrats.

3. Voter Persuasion \- because of their spending advantage Republicans are flooding airwaves, mailboxes, and social media, with disinformation. The Democratic persuasion program is overextended and struggling to contain the GOPs massive breakthrough with has no resources to go on the offensive.

There is however a tangible path for Democrats to regain our advantage on each of these fronts and mount a comeback.
Defend Our Courts, the Democratic organization coordinating the defense of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court's liberal majority, is working to contest the GOP on each of these fronts but we need to rapidly scale our program in the remaining 25 days until election day.
The short runway and millions that will be required to salvage this race may seem daunting but our movement has done it in the past and we can do it again.
In 2021, millions of Democrats from across the nation poured in small dollar donations to support Senators Ossoff and Warnock pull off stunning victories in the Georgia Senate runoffs. And in Spring 2025, Dems rallied around the Wisconsin State Supreme Court race, a race with near identical stakes to ours, and successfully outraised and defeated Elon Musk and MAGA.

If we lose this court, MAGA will seize control of Pennsylvania and will implement an extreme abortion ban, redistrict the PA congressional map making it blood red, and rig the '26 midterms and '28 presidential in the penultimate swing state - 19 electoral college votes down the drain. Republicans pulled off a shocking lightning breakthrough last month and early polling now shows that a catastrophic loss is exactly what Democrats are on track for. These three factors explain why the GOP is winning: 1. If these trends continue they will surpass Democrats before our November 4th Election Day. 2. The short runway and millions that will be required to salvage this race may seem daunting but our movement has done it in the past and we can do it again. * * *
So Donald Trump finally got the Department of Justice to indict New York Attorney General Letitia James on these bullshit fraud charges. Obviously, it's part of his broader revenge tour--going after anyone who's ever crossed him or poses a threat to whatever dystopian nightmare he's trying to turn this country into.
He's going after James Comey. He's going after Adam Schiff. He's going after ActBlue and key pieces of the Democratic Party's infrastructure. He's gone after lawyers. Comedians. Harvard. Whole institutions--demanding loyalty pledges like he's some wannabe emperor of academia.
And still, according to most of the traditional media and _literally_ the entire Republican Party, we're not allowed to call this fascism. We're the ones who are "inappropriate" for pointing out that this is what fascism looks like. That these are the actions of a man who wants to rule as an authoritarian.
And here's the thing: this is going to keep getting worse before it gets better. Because neither Congress nor the courts seem willing to stand up to a president who's losing popularity but gaining power. He keeps testing the boundaries--reaching out and poking at the walls of democracy we all assumed were stone, only to realize they're paper.
The rumor mill is wild right now about who's next. They want to take down George Soros. They want to destroy Indivisible--the group helping organize street-level resistance. They want to go after political operatives, activists, anyone with a voice that stands in opposition to this president.
* * *

Paid subscribers make it all possible--just $8/month if you're down to support](https://substack.com/redirect/5e6fde58-d890-4c90-90e5-4c92daeba3a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): **_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/5e6fde58-d890-4c90-90e5-4c92daeba3a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Look at what they did to John Bolton. That raid wasn't just about embarrassing a Trump critic--it was about silencing someone who dared call out Trump's foreign policy, especially around Russia and Ukraine. And let's not forget: during his campaign, Trump openly promised political revenge. Most people didn't take it seriously. His base thought he'd focus on their problems.
But once in power, it's clear--he's only focused on _his_ problems. On flexing. On punishing. On ICE terrorizing cities like Chicago. On building monuments to himself in D.C. He's not doing anything to help you.
He's not using that power to make groceries cheaper. Or rent. Or health insurance. But he'll absolutely use it to go after comedians who made a joke he didn't like. He'll use it to tear down the infrastructure that helps his opposition win elections.
And Democrats _have_ been winning this year. That's part of what this is. What's happening to Tish James, Comey, Schiff--it's dangerous. Most of it will probably get tossed out in court, and that's the point. He wants the spectacle. He wants to drain them dry--money, energy, reputation--while they fight bogus charges.
Maybe he'll get some convictions. I doubt it. And even if he does, they'll be garbage--eventually overturned. The Comey charges are especially ridiculous. But it won't stop him. This is lawfare--exactly what Republicans accused Democrats of. It's a calculated, relentless assault to bleed the other side dry.
And it's only going to escalate--just like what's happening in Chicago. Every day, they get more brazen. Yes, they're getting less popular--and that _does_ matter. We've got an election in 2026, and if we can keep it free and fair, we're going to win. I believe we've got a fighting shot in 2028 too. Because the country doesn't like this.
They might not love Democrats--but they hate _this_. Most Americans want a government that works for them, and it's crystal clear this one doesn't.
It's a scary time. I keep coming back to something I said yesterday: I know that feeling of apathy. That tight-chested rage. That feeling of being overwhelmed. They _want_ you to feel that way. Too much news. Too much chaos. It's by design.
But you've got to find your lane and be useful. We all carry different weights--but keep moving. One step at a time. Be helpful where you can. We can't control the White House. We can't control Congress. But we can control our response.
We can show up--like at the No Kings Rally on October 18th. We can call our reps--_especially_ Republicans--and demand they extend ACA premium subsidies and end the shutdown. We can organize locally. We can look out for our neighbors.
I saw a video this morning of a woman being dragged from her car during school pickup by ICE. Horrific. But also? A lot of parents in Chicago are stepping up--making sure kids get to school, making sure families aren't left alone. That's the work.
This isn't how a free society is supposed to operate--but it's how it operates under Trump.
So figure out how you can be useful. Because we need you. Take care of yourself. Stay alert. And God love you.
--Mike
P.S. Don't let the bastards grind you down.

Trump's revenge tour has entered a dangerous new phase. | | | Oct 10 | | | | | | | | | | | | : So Donald Trump finally got the Department of Justice to indict New York Attorney General Letitia James on these bullshit fraud charges. Obviously, it's part of his broader revenge tour--going after anyone who's ever crossed him or poses a threat to whatever dystopian nightmare he's trying to turn this country into. He's going after James Comey. He's going after Adam Schiff. He's going after ActBlue and key pieces of the Democratic Party's infrastructure. He's gone after lawyers. Comedians. Harvard. Whole institutions--demanding loyalty pledges like he's some wannabe emperor of academia. And still, according to most of the traditional media and literally the entire Republican Party, we're not allowed to call this fascism. We're the ones who are "inappropriate" for pointing out that this is what fascism looks like. That these are the actions of a man who wants to rule as an authoritarian. And here's the thing: this is going to keep getting worse before it gets better. Because neither Congress nor the courts seem willing to stand up to a president who's losing popularity but gaining power. He keeps testing the boundaries--reaching out and poking at the walls of democracy we all assumed were stone, only to realize they're paper. The rumor mill is wild right now about who's next. They want to take down George Soros. They want to destroy Indivisible--the group helping organize street-level resistance. They want to go after political operatives, activists, anyone with a voice that stands in opposition to this president. : * Look at what they did to John Bolton. That raid wasn't just about embarrassing a Trump critic--it was about silencing someone who dared call out Trump's foreign policy, especially around Russia and Ukraine. And let's not forget: during his campaign, Trump openly promised political revenge. Most people didn't take it seriously. His base thought he'd focus on their problems. But once in power, it's clear--he's only focused on his problems. On flexing. On punishing. On ICE terrorizing cities like Chicago. On building monuments to himself in D.C. He's not doing anything to help you. He's not using that power to make groceries cheaper. Or rent. Or health insurance. But he'll absolutely use it to go after comedians who made a joke he didn't like. He'll use it to tear down the infrastructure that helps his opposition win elections. And Democrats have been winning this year. That's part of what this is. What's happening to Tish James, Comey, Schiff--it's dangerous. Most of it will probably get tossed out in court, and that's the point. He wants the spectacle. He wants to drain them dry--money, energy, reputation--while they fight bogus charges. Maybe he'll get some convictions. I doubt it. And even if he does, they'll be garbage--eventually overturned. The Comey charges are especially ridiculous. But it won't stop him. This is lawfare--exactly what Republicans accused Democrats of. It's a calculated, relentless assault to bleed the other side dry. And it's only going to escalate--just like what's happening in Chicago. Every day, they get more brazen. Yes, they're getting less popular--and that does matter. We've got an election in 2026, and if we can keep it free and fair, we're going to win. I believe we've got a fighting shot in 2028 too. Because the country doesn't like this. They might not love Democrats--but they hate this. Most Americans want a government that works for them, and it's crystal clear this one doesn't. It's a scary time. I keep coming back to something I said yesterday: I know that feeling of apathy. That tight-chested rage. That feeling of being overwhelmed. They want you to feel that way. Too much news. Too much chaos. It's by design. But you've got to find your lane and be useful. We all carry different weights--but keep moving. One step at a time. Be helpful where you can. We can't control the White House. We can't control Congress. But we can control our response. We can show up--like at the No Kings Rally on October 18th. We can call our reps--especially Republicans--and demand they extend ACA premium subsidies and end the shutdown. We can organize locally. We can look out for our neighbors. I saw a video this morning of a woman being dragged from her car during school pickup by ICE. Horrific. But also? A lot of parents in Chicago are stepping up--making sure kids get to school, making sure families aren't left alone. That's the work. This isn't how a free society is supposed to operate--but it's how it operates under Trump. So figure out how you can be useful. Because we need you. Take care of yourself. Stay alert. And God love you. --Mike P.S. Don't let the bastards grind you down. Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. He 's the founder of Authentic.org, an award-winning fundraising and advertising agency, and a former Senior Advisor to Vice President Kamala Harris. clean_body: Our work to keep moving Arizona forward has only just begun, and the stakes in this race are sky-high. | | Team, it 's Katie. I wanted you to hear it from me first: I'm officially running for re-election as governor of Arizona. I 'm running to serve you for four more years because our work to deliver on the Arizona Promise has only just begun. From cutting taxes for middle-class families, small businesses, and veterans, to lowering childcare costs, to erasing medical debt for over 350,000 Arizonans, I'm focused on creating real solutions for our state's toughest challenges - unlike the Washington politicians who prefer to play partisan games. I'm proud to be the first social worker ever elected governor in this country. Arizonans don't need out-of-touch, career politicians who care more about billionaires than working families - they deserve leaders who actually understand the struggles we face. I know what working families are going through -- because I've lived it. I grew up in a working-class family in the heart of Tempe. I worked at Burger King and Pizza Hut to put myself through school. I lost my home in the Great Recession. I drove for Uber to make ends meet. My husband and I are still paying off student loans. That 's why every decision I make as governor is about delivering real results for families, not playing Washington political games. But all our progress is on the line in this election. Donald Trump and National Republicans have made the Arizona governor's race one of their top targets to flip red in 2026, and they're prepared to spend whatever it takes to do it. It's why political experts at the Cook Political Report, Larry Sabato's Crystal Ball , and Inside Elections have already called this race a pure toss-up. It's why Trump has endorsed not one, but TWO of my three GOP opponents. But unlike my Trump-endorsed opponents, I don't have a vast personal fortune or far-right billionaires on speed dial. I have something far better: You. name: Justin Riemer - RITE President
subject: RITE Urges Supreme Court to Abandon Flawed Redistricting Criteria
body:
RITE asks Court to end the use of unworkable race-based tests |
---
| |
---
| | **RITE Urges Supreme Court to Abandon Flawed Redistricting Criteria**
**WASHINGTON, DC** – Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (“RITE”), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect the rule of law in elections, has filed an [amicus brief](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=a5f5e418b4&e=ea91f782ea) urging the U.S. Supreme Court to end the use of unworkable race-based judicial tests in redistricting cases brought under Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act.

Alabama’s 2020 decennial redistricting congressional maps have made multiple trips to the Supreme Court. This time, Alabama sought Supreme Court review after a three-judge district court panel ruled its 2023 remedial congressional map violated Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act by failing to create a second majority-minority district, even though doing so would have violated traditional districting principles.

For nearly forty years, courts have struggled to apply the nine-factor _Gingles_ test to vote-dilution racial gerrymandering claims. _Gingles_ has flummoxed courts and for good reason. As RITE’s brief explains, the test forces courts to make impossible political judgments about how much electoral power different racial groups “deserve.” Simultaneously, states must avoid considering race too much or risk violating the Fourteenth Amendment.

“Alabama’s case gives the Supreme Court a valuable opportunity to abandon the failed, unworkable _Gingles_ test that has wreaked havoc on state’s redistricting for too long,” said RITE President Justin Riemer. “It’s better to have no test than one that’s unmanageable and constitutionally suspect, and in any event, courts have other tools at their disposal to police actual racial gerrymandering. We urge the Supreme Court to reverse the district court’s flawed ruling.” ###

name: Britney VanCitters
subject: Are you registered to vote?
body:
https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/registration.aspx?lang=en [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/registration.aspx?lang=en]
Hi Peter,
It’s that time of the year again... We’re only a few days away from the voter registration deadline on Tuesday, October 14th! You may have an election coming up on November 4th, so it’s time to check your registration and make sure you’re ready to use your voice. Make sure you’re registered or check your registration here — it only takes a second! [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/registration.aspx?lang=en]
Register to vote [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/registration.aspx?lang=en]
With all the attacks on our democracy we’ve been seeing from the Trump Administration, it’s more important than ever for us to continue showing up and standing up for what’s right. Exercising your right to vote whenever possible, and to vote for climate action, is a perfect way to do just that! But, you won’t be able to take a stand unless your voter registration is correct.
Even if you haven’t recently moved or are sure that you’re registered to vote, it’s always a good idea to check your voter registration to make sure that you are ready to receive your ballot in a few days. Check your registration using My Vote here - it only takes a second! [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/myvote.aspx?lang=en]
Register to vote [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/registration.aspx?lang=en]
The Oregon My Vote [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/myvote.aspx?lang=en] system can also help you track the status of your ballot once it’s been mailed, locate your nearest ballot drop box, and look up contact information for your county election office - so be sure to save this website.
Thank you for taking part in our democracy,

| Friend,
The very fate of our Democracy and the electoral future of the Democratic party rests upon a Democratic victory in the sleepy and often overlooked 2025 Pennsylvania Supreme Court Retention Election.
If we lose this court, MAGA will seize control of Pennsylvania and will implement an extreme abortion ban, redistrict the PA congressional map making it blood red, and rig the '26 midterms and '28 presidential in the penultimate swing state - 19 electoral college votes down the drain.
Republicans pulled off a shocking lightning breakthrough last month and early polling now shows that a catastrophic loss is exactly what Democrats are on track for. These three factors explain why the GOP is winning:
---
| 1.) Voter registration \- over the Summer, the Pennsylvania GOP shrunk the million voter registration gap that Democrats once held over Republicans to just a 50,000 vote lead. If these trends continue they will surpass Democrats before our November 4th Election Day.
2.) Spending \- bankrolled by the likes of Jeff Yass, the richest man in Pennsylvania, Elon Musk, and Tristan Tate, accused human trafficker and brother of masculinity influencer Andrew Tate, the GOP effort to seize this court boasts a 10-1 spending advantage over Democrats.
3.) Voter Persuasion \- because of their spending advantage Republicans are flooding airwaves, mailboxes, and social media, with disinformation. The Democratic persuasion program is overextended and struggling to contain the GOPs massive breakthrough with has no resources to go on the offensive.
---
| There is however a tangible path for Democrats to regain our advantage on each of these fronts and mount a comeback.
Defend our Courts, the Democratic organization coordinating the defense of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court's liberal majority, is working to contest the GOP on each of these fronts but we need to rapidly scale our program in the remaining 25 days until election day.
The short runway and millions that will be required to salvage this race may seem daunting but our movement has done it in the past and we can do it again.
In 2021 millions of Democrats from across the nation poured in small dollar donations to support Senators Ossoff and Warnock pull off stunning victories in the Georgia Senate runoffs. And in Spring 2025, Dems rallied around the Wisconsin State Supreme Court race, a race with near identical stakes to ours, and successfully outraised and defeated Elon Musk and MAGA.
This is a desperate call for all Democrats to come to rally around Pennsylvania like we did Georgia and Wisconsin. [Can we count on you donate $50, $25, or even $5, to help prevent a catastrophic defeat and propel a historic Democratic win? name: James Talarico
subject: Taken for granted
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Talarico for Texas
body:
#
Peter —
A lot of campaigns talk about going everywhere and talking to everyone. Few actually do it.
That’s because going everywhere in a state as big as Texas is an investment — both in time and money.
But taking back Texas requires that kind of investment — **especially in South Texas.**
That’s why, just a few weeks into the campaign, I showed up in McAllen...
[](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251010-1-ak&t=1&akid=106%2E1347274%2EiFHhpF)
And Brownsville — deep in the heart of the Rio Grande Valley.
[](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251010-1-ak&t=2&akid=106%2E1347274%2EiFHhpF)
I also went to bright red Victoria — a community that voted for Trump in the last election by 40 points.
[](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251010-1-ak&t=3&akid=106%2E1347274%2EiFHhpF)
Campaigning in this part of the state was like a homecoming for me.
My granddad was a Baptist preacher in South Texas. My mom was born in Port Lavaca and raised in Laredo. And I still have family in the area.
**The truth is, DC politicians don’t understand South Texas.**
For too long, national Democrats have taken communities like this one for granted. So people in South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley were open to an alternative.
In the last election, Republican politicians showed up here and made big promises.
* They promised to make everything less expensive.
* They promised to put working families first.
* They promised to drain the swamp.

But look what’s happened since the last election:
* Everything is more expensive.
* Working families are falling further behind.
* And corruption in Washington is the worst it’s ever been.

We see it happening in real time. As we speak, DC Republicans like John Cornyn are trying to gut healthcare for millions of Texans so they can give another tax break to their donors. And they're willing to shut down the government to do it.
That means a mom in the Valley — working two jobs, raising three kids — won’t be able to afford her premiums. All so billionaires can make even more money.
Republican politicians promised big change but delivered more of the same.
**I told the people of South Texas: If you feel like you’ve been conned, if you feel like you’ve been let down by both political parties — you’ve got a place in this campaign.**
Thank you, South Texas, for showing up for us.
I’ll keep showing up for you.
James

Our campaign is going to go everywhere and talk to everyone. James knows that taking back Texas from billionaire mega-donors and their puppet politicians starts with showing up for the people.
But barnstorming the state is expensive. It’s a lot of ground to cover, and it would be impossible without small donations from people like you.
[**If you can, please consider making a donation of any amount to keep James on the road. Every dollar is immediately invested to lay the groundwork required to win this race.**](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251010-1-ak&t=4&akid=106%2E1347274%2EiFHhpF)
[DONATE](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251010-1-ak&t=5&akid=106%2E1347274%2EiFHhpF)

Austin, TX 78761

| | | | Dear Peter, Donald Trump just took another swing at Tennessee’s working families—and this time, he’s increasing your energy bill.
Instead of helping everyday Americans, Trump dismantled a program that had already been approved and funded—one that would have delivered over $150 million to help low-income Tennesseans install solar panels and lower their electricity bills.
Nationwide, nearly a million families were set to benefit. Now? That relief is gone. Possibly illegally. And we’re left wondering: where is that money going now?
Here’s the truth: Republicans aren’t interested in helping working people. They’re too busy enriching the Trump family and their political allies and protecting billionaire donors and corporate polluters. Meanwhile, Democrats in the Tennessee House are focused on the issues that matter—like keeping your utility bills low, preventing the privatization of TVA and fighting for real energy justice.
But we can’t do it alone.
Peter, we need your help right now. The 2026 midterms are approaching fast, and we’re fighting to make gerrymandered districts competitive and restore power to the people.
Will you chip in $20—or whatever you can—to help us fight back and support Democrats who stand with working families?

name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: From the Front with Patrick J. Murphy
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
Hey Friends,
Trying something new. Going forward, every Friday at noon, I’ll be sharing a quick update on what I’ve been doing and learning.
This week, I focused on trust .
As I wrote on Substack [https://patrickmurphypa.substack.com/p/americans-are-losing-trust-in-our] this week, “When the government shuts down — as it has ten times in the last fifty years [https://usafacts.org/articles/everything-you-need-to-know-about-a-government-shutdown/?utm_source=chatgpt.com] , including four under President Trump — it doesn’t just freeze budgets. It freezes faith. Faith in the idea that this country still works. It’s a failure of trust.”
Since 1976, we’ve seen 20 funding gaps, resulting in 10 government shutdowns. Every stalemate in Washington hurts real people: small-business owners, families living paycheck to paycheck, and, most criminally, veterans and military personnel waiting on benefits. Promises mean little if resources don’t reach those who served.
Leadership, Not Slogans
We need a new kind of patriotism rooted in service, empathy, and shared responsibility. Trust is rebuilt through service, one action, one community, one conversation at a time.
On Tuesday, I spoke at the U.S. Army War College in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, about how to live a purpose-driven life. The room was filled with soldiers, military spouses, and transitioning veterans — people who’ve served something larger than themselves. They understand something too many in Washington have forgotten: trust isn’t declared. It’s earned.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/Operation%20Freedom%2025.jpg]
Read the full essay on Substack → [https://patrickmurphypa.substack.com/] Americans Are Losing Trust in our Leaders. Here ́s How to Rebuild It [https://patrickmurphypa.substack.com/p/americans-are-losing-trust-in-our]
The Moral Failure in Washington
In the latest episode of Warrior Money , I discuss the brutal truth about veteran homelessness - 32,000 of my brother and sister veterans are homeless. This problem is not just a statistic, it’s a moral failure. We still have time to fix it.
On Faulkner Focus , I broke down the growing trust gap, warning that the political drama over the budget puts veterans & military families at risk. Congress and the White House need to prioritize real issues with real budget numbers and stop talking past each other. In an era where it’s easy to fall prey to cynicism, my takeaway is simple: trust in government will only return when leaders follow through on the needs of the people it serves. The government should not be an obstacle to those who sacrificed for it.
Watch my full appearance → Faulkner Focus [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nKX6QGFcrhE]
Watch the Warrior Money Clip → [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xbN3Zc2_EfE] Warrior Money Clip [https://finance.yahoo.com/video/military-families-survive-government-shutdown-190016986.html?soc_src=social-sh&soc_trk=ma]
Listen to the Full Episode → [https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/warrior-money/id1779749359] Episode: The brutal truth about veteran homelessness in America [https://finance.yahoo.com/video/brutal-truth-veteran-homelessness-america-190000167.html?soc_src=social-sh&soc_trk=ma]
The Throughline: Service Never Stops
Even when politics divides us, our shared purpose can unite us. Every conversation and act of service adds up. If we want to rebuild trust in America, don’t wait for those in Washington, it’ll happen in the small moments where we show up for each other.
Thank you for being part of our team.
Honorable Patrick J. Murphy
32nd Army Under Secretary

subject: President Trump is coming after Oregon right now. It could be Maryland's tomorrow.
body:
I’m standing up to Trump’s attack on Portland, but I need your support.
Peter,
A federal judge has blocked President Trump’s attempt to send military troops into Portland — _twice!_
But he’s not done attacking our state, so my work’s not done either. I’ll continue to stand up to his administration and protect Oregon values. [**Will you split a donation between Wes Moore and myself to help us keep up the fight?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20251010-1.XDIfHO&refcode=em-20251010-1&t=1&akid=739%2E1086043%2EN5XpGt)**
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20251010-1.XDIfHO&amount=10&refcode=em-20251010-1&t=2&akid=739%2E1086043%2EN5XpGt)**
Trump’s attacks on Portland, as well as similar ones in Los Angeles, Chicago, and Washington, D.C., are unwarranted and unlawful, Peter. We cannot normalize these escalating attempts to use the military to occupy our cities.
There is no need for military intervention in Oregon. The biggest threat to our public safety and our democracy is Donald Trump himself. I am committed to speaking out, standing with the people of Oregon, and solving the _real_ problems facing our state.
**[I need you with us in this fight, Peter. Will you donate $10 split between Wes Moore and myself to help us stand against Donald Trump’s unlawful military intervention?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20251010-1.XDIfHO&refcode=em-20251010-1&t=3&akid=739%2E1086043%2EN5XpGt)**

If you are scared or angry (or both) about what President Trump’s actions mean for our country and our democracy, know that I’m fighting for you and with you.
Thank you for standing with me.
— Tina Kotek

Patriot, When I heard of Charlie Kirk, he wasn't famous. He wasn't filling arenas. He wasn't a household name. A few people told me, _" You've gotta meet this guy -- he's doing something big out in Illinois."_ So I went. Charlie was running Turning Point from a modest office in the Chicago suburbs -- surviving on coffee and pure belief that America was still worth saving.
[ ](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=033a8e78d2814e0a8ef0189bc8af0f62&_e=xneePAfplkLWUceiGL35etgaTjwzTAsmzdPlnJeWsVsdjz-BjLLC3Yj7-14t9sFzPqv-y0P8pH9SVD8-ZjvWybRUtenPlXRhtWt4dxYGLnQfnNjj5HZgusC8wx1_TtF8AF-MFZEblKWQth9hsHkdUDJmj_rXJ5nmvfYU69edn7SCsUjXvKYhpB2fIz60Lr_1PXQOA-OCyitydFo4X0HqMTxd7sB1Q50zjgbDahYP8W0keUX8H2IkwOizzgKrxwKhXPVruBzn28JYwfKOtLpP2n03714md_KMfqqBo2l7u5QZKizClLKMmN9BH5FhKk4gHRtuOcnNxNTuam_q4lLOrxDR0NpjRZnRkg-oQGA8J9kjcqOG_4TQI0pFt-f-o5gKlKojhLNxHT0gay6g9mW7xWnUU7Rq8HCXNDO9LO-zXVgCAdnHJFtewMT3ekKFpGKfBdupD2FbT-JUWWvxN5S9mk-_YWXC5OX9HDKWx6QUSy5-tu4EPgIZC9kkcU6xsC4GzqiarOEEjofCTuD61WROdMQVzCCeXPr3LmI323HUVkPO1h25UViVkLN9eN1Xk55HH6RjKAs2bzMfLC8NZXOwJ6_hKrdI3JUBiwTjxQbn5RrxrlHbWfbTYAhM7RO1-YUwN4J3TZ1d45b3pn-3TaQN3pbDRrVohvLvScCJdEqQ_SgfRdhZu3Jr1V2tfGN3R5uAyOtGRl5PGsbf02Q-TxYLs5oMJ8j3F0eGIs8aiEWPtG0%3D)
_**Above:** The original Turning Point HQ in Lemont, Illinois. This is where it all began -- just Charlie, a vision, and a mission that changed everything. _
Back then, we were both organizing young conservatives, both dreaming about how to win back the culture. But when I first sat down with Charlie... _I knew._ Charlie was the visionary. He had the plan. And I HAD to be part of it. I jumped in and never looked back. From that moment on, I was there for all of it. The early conferences and campuses. The road trips. The rallies. The fights. In those days, our team didn't have much. But what we had was conviction -- and that was more than enough. Because we believed in something BIG. Something real. Something urgent. **Faith, family, freedom** -- and the absolute grit to go build something that could save this country. And Charlie? _He did it._ He didn't just build a brand... _He built a machine._ First, Charlie built a movement that changed the hearts and minds of an entire generation -- a seismic shift that flipped the narrative that young people belonged to the Left. Then, he built Turning Point Action to become the grassroots force the Left never saw coming... and beat them at their own game. And, I hitched my wagon to it _from the start._ Charlie and I weren't just friends... We were brothers in the fight. We did everything together.
[ ](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=033a8e78d2814e0a8ef0189bc8af0f62&_e=xneePAfplkLWUceiGL35etgaTjwzTAsmzdPlnJeWsVsdjz-BjLLC3Yj7-14t9sFzPqv-y0P8pH9SVD8-ZjvWybRUtenPlXRhtWt4dxYGLnQfnNjj5HZgusC8wx1_TtF8AF-MFZEblKWQth9hsHkdUDJmj_rXJ5nmvfYU69edn7SCsUjXvKYhpB2fIz60Lr_1PXQOA-OCyitydFo4X0HqMTxd7sB1Q50zjgbDahYP8W0keUX8H2IkwOizzgKrxwKhvjCvgQzahGqlrg4j74gxzFjYJJlXiF-ShVDlkF9XbXGaDdr1FNdiToAmfCP0VFYtRlDGLmLPNXF9zl2kwlJ4uC_rSKfNTi916VN-s25PuwIDiYJGZf5rQuoM3w-zFF49LRkYygii0PWiALtbvyOa0Z8ja5BGU61rjLB4c-RDpa_oI2AFV_u6xCVq-7LeFSxcBIe3sQBFwxqeJywoWiT09ZpMacgL_f4UGmv1ywHn_0r7_Ds9sM6MSW6xBe-KZMWuyicrRfnvxMSjeCB93FBdVkAJBkfgeP_usV5wBTrVD0kAB2egjI5zCAcC6rsJF05OxpjlDYQl0jRSy08OHT8TaR_q8mNokEO5HqhuDd8sjs8iyYjzmtugEcbW55k0myfI-kJ85oOqCVXkzmHh1yJVJZpM-7EmBRM5mk-5d5HvygcEN8XYsdLwXFjdDu5eFbSU1-I33bYEmD9LMOGZRCnADsdoHnAQ_cfdy4FQ76qs1zo%3D)
We strategized over midnight texts... battled together through COVID, the 2020 Election, and every crisis they threw at us... We created AmericaFest from scratch... launched Turning Point Action to go on offense -- in the very states the GOP had given up on. **And we rallied a grassroots army that put President Donald J. Trump back in the White House in 2024. ** We didn't just talk about chasing ballots... Turning Point Action built the first full-scale, professional ballot-chasing operation on the Right -- _and it delivered real results._ 10 for 10. **In every single state we operated in... Trump won.** In Arizona _alone,_ we chased over 205,000 low-propensity conservative votes -- well beyond the margin of victory. _In Wisconsin?_ 60,000+. _In Nevada?_ 6,000+ -- and we won back a district we hadn't carried in 20 years. _In Michigan?_ 14,000+ votes helped us flip a U.S. House seat and take the state house majority. We didn't just make noise... _We made history. _
