Peter, Did you know that Mecklenburg County — a smaller county than Wake — has _twice_ as many prosecutors? That’s a big problem. Here in Wake County, our District Attorney’s office is stretched too thin. That means victims have to wait years rather than months for justice and repeat offenders stay on the streets longer in Wake. **When prosecutors are overworked and under-resourced, everyone in our community is less safe.** The numbers tell the story: Mecklenburg County has 94 prosecutors. Wake County? Just 43. And when you factor in that Wake County has grown by more than 35% over the past 15 years (from about 900,000 residents to more than 1.2 million) but our DA’s office hasn’t grown with it, it's clear why we’re falling behind. We simply can’t keep up with public safety demands without expanding the team that prosecutes violent crime and protects our families. As a former Congressman and State Senator, I know how to bring results and resources back to Wake County. As your next District Attorney, I’ll fight to double the size of our DA’s office, support law enforcement, and make sure justice is delivered fairly and efficiently. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117052603/575193213/-1650971833?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20251010_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMjE1NzdlYS0yMGE2LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vqGVZmsTMSJm8qf09iXQv5OYxw5_yH3AfempGsvPZAI=) I’m running for District Attorney because the prosecutors in Wake County are dedicated public servants doing an incredible job under tough conditions. They deserve a DA who will have their back — and the resources to get the job done. This campaign is about standing up for law enforcement, ensuring justice for victims, and building a safer Wake County for everyone. clean_body: Mecklenburg has twice as many prosecutors as Wake County | Peter, Did you know that Mecklenburg County — a smaller county than Wake — has twice as many prosecutors? That’s a big problem. Here in Wake County, our District Attorney’s office is stretched too thin. That means victims have to wait years rather than months for justice and repeat offenders stay on the streets longer in Wake. When prosecutors are overworked and under-resourced, everyone in our community is less safe. The numbers tell the story: Mecklenburg County has 94 prosecutors. Wake County? Just 43. And when you factor in that Wake County has grown by more than 35% over the past 15 years (from about 900,000 residents to more than 1.2 million) but our DA’s office hasn’t grown with it, it's clear why we’re falling behind. We simply can’t keep up with public safety demands without expanding the team that prosecutes violent crime and protects our families. As a former Congressman and State Senator, I know how to bring results and resources back to Wake County. As your next District Attorney, I’ll fight to double the size of our DA’s office, support law enforcement, and make sure justice is delivered fairly and efficiently. = I’m running for District Attorney because the prosecutors in Wake County are dedicated public servants doing an incredible job under tough conditions. They deserve a DA who will have their back — and the resources to get the job done. [1]Justice Democrats

Can you feel the momentum, Peter?

We just announced our third 2026 Democratic primary endorsement on
Wednesday, and the news is already making waves:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251010.zzRj4P&refcode=em20251010-37098&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37098%2E1203867%2EdVTLKH ]Rolling Stone article headline. At the top, the red Rolling Stone logo
appears, with a red label beneath it that says “NEW WAVE.” The headline
reads: “JUSTIN J. PEARSON OF THE ‘TENNESSEE THREE’ HAS HAD IT WITH
‘MEDIOCRITY’ — SO HE’S RUNNING FOR CONGRESS.” Below the headline, a
subheading says: “'Things are not normal,' the 30-year-old Memphis native
tells Rolling Stone.”

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251010.zzRj4P&refcode=em20251010-37098&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37098%2E1203867%2EdVTLKH ]A tweet from ABC News (@ABC) reads: “Tennessee state Rep. Justin
Pearson, a 30-year-old progressive activist and lawmaker who gained
national attention as one of the 'Tennessee Three,' is launching a primary
challenge against longtime Democratic Rep. Steve Cohen.”

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251010.zzRj4P&refcode=em20251010-37098&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=37098%2E1203867%2EdVTLKH ]Screenshot of an article from The Nation reading: “Why Justin Pearson
Wants to Unseat a 10-Term Democratic Incumbent in Congress.” The
subheading says: “The Tennessee state representative explains why he is
facing off against Steve Cohen to be the Democratic nominee to represent
the Memphis area in Washington.”

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251010.zzRj4P&refcode=em20251010-37098&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1005&akid=37098%2E1203867%2EdVTLKH ]Screenshot from Common Dreams with the headline: ‘This Moment Calls for
a True Fighter’: Progressive Group Backs Justin Pearson for Congress.
Below the headline, the quote reads: “Justice Democrats is so proud to
endorse Justin J. Pearson to bring people-first leadership to Tennessee’s
only Democratic district,” said the group’s executive director.

Justin J. Pearson is the real deal. If elected, he’ll:

* Bring justice to working families and make life more affordable for
everyday people by taking on billionaires like Elon Musk and Trump;
* Deliver environmental justice to a community poisoned by corporations
like Musk’s xAI plant;
* End the scourge of gun violence that he has proved willing to
sacrifice his own seat in office for;
* Fight back against GOP cuts to Medicaid and Medicare by ensuring
healthcare is a right, not a privilege, with Medicare for All;
* Stand up to Trump’s National Guard and federal troop takeover with
more than Congressional statements and tweets.

But in order for him to take on a powerful career politician and win his
primary next August, he needs YOU to help lay the foundation today.

Peter,
Imagine a country where you can't put your children to bed, head to bed yourself, and not be awoken in the middle of the night by loud noises, screaming, and federal agents pounding at the door. They break down your door, throw you into the street, zip tie your family -even your young children. Outside are your neighbors, some of them naked. Citizens and non-citizens alike are loaded into unmarked vans while your apartment is ransacked. Because right now this is not a hypothetical country. This is America. And it happened in Chicago earlier this month. Our Constitutional rights are being trampled on before our very eyes. The people in that apartment building were rounded up like animals and denied due process. They can do the same to ANYONE. They already are. In Trump's hands, DHS - and particularly ICE - has become a Gestapo police agency. ICE's new bloated budget, larger than most standing armies, is now functioning as the President's private paramilitary force. So why does our Democratic congresswoman, my opponent Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, keep voting to expand their power? Marie has not only repeatedly voted to increase ICE's funding, she voted for the Laken Riley Act - the bill that laid the foundation for Trump's anti-immigrant agenda. She even signed a resolution "thanking" ICE for a job well done earlier _this year_ , as illegal raids ramped up, families were separated, and community members thrown in the back of vans by masked, unidentified men. **Marie is not willing to fight back against Trump 's deportation machine, and she clearly doesn't understand the stakes of this moment. This is what Marie has invited into our own backyard with her votes and her Republican complicity. We need representatives who stand up to these gross abuses of power. When I get to Congress, I am going to fight like hell to shut down ICE's insane "enforcement" actions. body:
Republicans are punishing the people who defend this country.

| | It's Gabe Vasquez. Right now, our troops are on the verge of missing paychecks due to the government shutdown, and Speaker Mike Johnson isn’t lifting a finger to stop it. That's why I sent a letter demanding that the Speaker call the House back before October 15 to pass a bill that pays our service members. **Plain and simple**. But instead of working with Democrats towards a solution, Speaker Johnson and this extreme MAGA-led House are on a campaign to hurt as many people as possible because they’re not getting their way. They’re already targeting our health care, they’ve already walked away from budget talks, and now, they’re putting our military families on the line. Republicans and Donald Trump might see our troops as political pawns. But we see them for who they are: **heroes who deserve respect, and most of all, a paycheck**. This is the fight we’re in. And it’s why 2026 matters. We need a House that works for its people, its service members, and its democracy — not one that only answers to Donald Trump. In this fight together, Gabe

name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: I just held a town hall in Germany. Here’s what I heard:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY POWERED BY PEOPLE
body:
[1]Powered By People

I just had the chance to hold a public town hall meeting with a group of
Americans in Berlin—people who may live far from home, but who still care
deeply about the future of our country.

We talked about what’s happening in the U.S. right now—a president who’s
defied the Constitution, ignored federal court orders, dismantled agencies
meant to serve people, slashed health care for millions, and even demanded
that Texas redraw its maps to steal five House seats and attempt to hang
on to the House of Representatives.

Trump is consolidating power because he knows that if he loses control of
the House or Senate in 2026, there will be a check on his lawlessness and
corruption. He’ll be held accountable—and there will finally be the
possibility of free and fair elections again.

But as I told everyone in that room in Germany earlier this week: It’s on
each and every one of us to do what we can with what we have where we are.

I’ve held these kinds of all-comers welcome town hall meetings in every
part of Texas and all across the country. My favorite conversations are
with people—no matter their party—who come together in unlikely places to
talk about what matters most to them. Because that’s where democracy
really lives: in our willingness to show up, to listen, and to act
together.

That’s exactly what we’re doing each day through Powered by
People—organizing in every region of Texas, registering new voters, and
building the infrastructure that ensures every voice is heard. When we
show up, we create the conditions for free and fair elections, a
government that delivers for the people, and a democracy that works for
all of us.

Here’s the reality: too many people back home don’t feel like they have a
future where they can succeed. They’re struggling to afford childcare,
health care, housing, education, and even a healthy meal—in the
wealthiest, most powerful nation on the planet.

We don’t lack the resources to do what’s right. We’re just up against
forces more concerned with holding on to power than serving the people.

That’s what we’re working to change. By organizing, mobilizing,
registering voters, and delivering for people, we will prove that
democracy can work, that government can make life better, and that our
party can be the one that gets things done.

If we do that—if we deliver—we can transform this country.

| | Hi, it’s Oregon Secretary of State, Tobias Read.
When President Trump’s Department of Justice demanded Oregon’s complete voter-registration data, including driver’s license numbers and parts of Social Security numbers. **I had one response:****No way! **
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117055194/575200607/-1348697765?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NTgxZjhkOS0yOWE2LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iswsMuhBetiWwW3TpiBp77-d-zcbv2-wNoQHOmf6mt8=&emci=7f81f8d9-29a6-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=8581f8d9-29a6-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=30662126)

Not to any President! ** My job is to protect both your right to vote and your right to privacy. clean_body: Private data belongs to Oregonians, not Donald Trump. | | | = | | Hi, it’s Oregon Secretary of State, Tobias Read. When President Trump’s Department of Justice demanded Oregon’s complete voter-registration data, including driver’s license numbers and parts of Social Security numbers. I had one response:No way! Oregon already provides the public voter information that’s required by law. But private data belongs to Oregonians, not President Trump. Not to any President! My job is to protect both your right to vote and your right to privacy. So for me, this isn’t about politics — it’s about principle. If we allow sensitive voter information to be handed over once, we open the door to misuse and distrust in our elections. That’s not how Oregon does things. We’ve built one of the most secure and transparent election systems in the country by earning voters’ trust. Let’s keep it that way. Attorney General Pam Bondi appeared at her first oversight hearing after nine months of her stewardship of the Justice Department.

It was urgent — after all, hundreds of career prosecutors have quit because of the politicization of the Justice Department and the fear that they might have to take unethical actions at the direction of Trump and Bondi.

We’ve seen the DOJ cover up the corruption of the administration and its friends — like the WH Border Czar taking $50,000 in cash from undercover FBI agents. Or the corruption case against the Mayor of NYC. Or the Epstein files.

And we’ve seen the department prosecute the president’s enemies at the president’s urging — like James Comey — even though career prosecutors said the case lacked evidence.

Peter, it’s safe to say Pam Bondi was not too pleased with my line of questioning. Don’t just take it from me, look at some of the headlines from the hearing: **[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/117055325/575201055/2088414854?amount=10&refcode=DOTL_20251010_EMSPL_E2_T0_AC&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNS8xLzk0MjI1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjVjYzcxOGMzLTJhYTYtZjAxMS04ZTYxLTYwNDViZGVkOGJhNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=abEIiAxxchGbGpWJHwP7OSnXn7f4BYZCqShrjHDTxqg=)** Peter, the Department of Justice has become Trump’s personal sword to go after his ever-growing list of political enemies, including me. And his shield to cover up corruption and hide wrongdoing.

And Pam Bondi has enabled this behavior.

Instead of going after Tom Homan, Trump’s border czar, for taking the 50 thousand in cash, the DOJ shut down the investigation.

When I asked Attorney General Bondi about this, she deflected responsibility. Said she didn’t know or wouldn’t comment about the case. She said that I should be**fired**. _Peter, she even said I should apologize to Donald Trump for leading his first impeachment trial._

_Not gonna happen._

The Department of Justice should be pursuing accountability, cracking down on corruption, and defending the Constitution. But under this administration, the DOJ is a tool for attacking enemies and covering up wrongdoing.

I will continue to use my position on the Judiciary Committee to conduct hard oversight and demand concrete answers. I will call out corruption and speak out against any and every attempt to weaponize our legal system against Trump’s political opponents. I will not give in, and not back down.

name: Tom Fitton
subject: Election Integrity Update!
body:
Voting Machine Vulnerabilities

[INSIDE JW]

SUPREME COURT HEARS ORAL ARGUMENTS IN HISTORIC ILLINOIS ELECTION
INTEGRITY CASE

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77116&L=36271&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dWJlLmNvbS9saXZlLzNOeWJ6WUlSV2ZNP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=dac5c66b3e8d33b06c5c98d5ce8628def73ffadfc4ed5fc864f0ca5730abcc7c]

The U.S. Supreme Court heard oral arguments
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77116&L=35864&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc3VwcmVtZWNvdXJ0Lmdvdi9vcmFsX2FyZ3VtZW50cy9hcmd1bWVudF9jYWxlbmRhcnMvTW9udGhseUFyZ3VtZW50Q2FsT2N0b2JlcjIwMjUucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=1549905422797a4d5bf7e8a1fb1ccb4f21b70414ce4ce0ebbc6ac18508e5fead]
this week in the historic case we filed on behalf of Congressman Mike
Bost and two presidential electors.

We were before the court to vindicate their standing to challenge an
Illinois law allowing the counting of ballots received up to 14 days
after the Election Day as set by federal law (_Rep. Michael J. Bost,
Laura Pollastrini, and Susan Sweeney v. The Illinois State Board of
Elections and Bernadette Matthews_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77116&L=28345&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21pY2hhZWwtYm9zdC1ldC1hbC12LWlsLWJvYXJkLW9mLWVsZWN0aW9ucy1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDI3NTQvXV8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=f4376e8898ff95bf9e3947157b9ae5b6c5656a891d5567d3dadc20895ed43f3c
_(No.
1:22-cv-02754, 23-2644, 24-568)).

We initially filed
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77116&L=27407&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbGF3c3VpdC1hZ2FpbnN0LWlsbGlub2lzLXRvLXN0b3AtY291bnRpbmctb2YtYmFsbG90cy1hZnRlci1lbGVjdGlvbi1kYXkvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=1b8b2e7ef9a18e3f797a44d49d3fad7b007089973d519a020f4f559472dd9712]
the lawsuit on May 25, 2022. A lower court dismissed the claim for
lack of standing, which was upheld by a split 2-1 panel for the U.S.
Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit.

This is the most important Supreme Court election law case in a
generation. Too many courts have denied candidates their right to
challenge unlawful election rules such as the outrageous act of
counting ballots that arrive AFTER Election Day. We will keep you
informed of all the developments in this case.

Our September brief
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77116&L=36162&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaWxsaW5vaXMtZWxlY3Rpb24taW50ZWdyaXR5LWNhc2UvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=7ec340c1c45b5426f39cf23210585c68450f4452e75ca763d088f8472065ae02]
to
the High Court states:

> Illinois counts mail-in ballots received up to two weeks after
> Election Day. Petitioners, candidates for federal office, claim that
> under controlling federal law that is two weeks too long. As a
> result, Illinois is counting unlawful ballots and producing
> inaccurate vote tallies, while simultaneously hurting petitioners’
> prospects at the ballot box and injuring their pocketbooks.

We submit that the Seventh Circuit’s decision is wrong and
dangerous:

> It is wrong because candidates have standing to challenge the rules
> that govern their elections, especially when their merits theory
> (which must be credited for standing purposes) is that the
> challenged rule produces an inaccurate final tally. At a minimum,
> the candidate has standing when (as here) he plausibly alleges that
> the challenged rule will harm his electoral prospects and reduce his
> bank balance because he needs to pay campaign staff an extra two
> weeks. And the decision is dangerous because it forces judges to
> play political prognosticators, skews standing rules to favor
> certain kinds of candidates, and funnels election disputes to the
> worst possible context—namely, after the election where judges are
> asked to declare political winners. This Court should reverse.

We state that Bost has standing to challenge the Illinois law:

> At the very least, Congressman Bost has standing to challenge the
> Illinois ballot-receipt deadline here, as a host of diverse _amici_
> confirm. Congressman Bost plausibly alleged a substantial risk that
> counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day will harm his
> electoral prospects both by risking electoral defeat and reducing
> his margin of victory. The plausibility of those allegations was
> amply reinforced by the Illinois Democratic Party’s attempted
> intervention and voting and litigation patterns nationwide. And he
> has also plausibly alleged a classic pocketbook injury because he
> expended additional campaign funds as a direct result of the
> state’s extended deadline for receiving mail-in ballots. Here
> too, the notion that an election artificially extended a fortnight
> costs more than one that ends on Election Day hardly strains
> credulity. The state’s contrary arguments lack merit.

In our previous Supreme Court brief
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77116&L=35884&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvc2NvdHVzLXBvc3QtZWxlY3Rpb24tYmFsbG90LWNvdW50aW5nLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=b1643502fff09f0ca65f7a5174c470ccef56502a1f4aa4ab5915468da5c944df],
we stated:

> Federal law sets the first Tuesday after the first Monday in
> November as the federal Election Day.

***

> Candidates have an obvious interest in the lawfulness and fairness
> of the rules that govern the elections into which they pour their
> time and resources. They also have an obvious interest “in
> ensuring that the final vote tally accurately reflects the legally
> valid votes cast.”

***

> Candidates pour enormous resources into running for election and
> have an obvious interest in the rules that dictate how long their
> races will last and how the ballots will be counted. They also have
> a distinct interest “in ensuring that the final vote tally
> accurately reflects the legally valid votes cast.”

We are a national leader
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77116&L=35695&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdGFnL2VsZWN0aW9uK2xhdy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=9397a9e3d745abe0c3f21cda7e7ee80355607c49f190c9e5632b403f671aff4b]
in voting integrity
and voting rights. As part of our work, we have assembled a team of
highly experienced voting rights attorneys.

Robert Popper, a Judicial Watch senior attorney, leads our election
law program. Popper was previously in the Voting Section of the Civil
Rights Division of the Justice Department, where he managed voting
rights investigations, litigations, consent decrees, and settlements
in dozens of states.

Paul Clement, who has argued more than 100 cases before the Supreme
Court, is representing Congressman Bost and the electors with us
before the Supreme Court. Clement is former solicitor general under
President George W. Bush from 2005-2008 and is widely regarded as
among the top Supreme Court litigators in the country.

T. Russell Nobile, a Judicial Watch senior attorney, is part of
Judicial Watch’s voting integrity efforts and focuses on campaign

clean_body: Voting Machine Vulnerabilities [INSIDE JW] SUPREME COURT HEARS ORAL ARGUMENTS IN HISTORIC ILLINOIS ELECTION INTEGRITY CASE [] The U.S. Supreme Court heard oral arguments [] this week in the historic case we filed on behalf of Congressman Mike Bost and two presidential electors. We were before the court to vindicate their standing to challenge an Illinois law allowing the counting of ballots received up to 14 days after the Election Day as set by federal law (Rep. Michael J. Bost, Laura Pollastrini, and Susan Sweeney v. The Illinois State Board of Elections and Bernadette Matthews [ (No. 1:22-cv-02754, 23-2644, 24-568)). We initially filed [] the lawsuit on May 25, 2022. A lower court dismissed the claim for lack of standing, which was upheld by a split 2-1 panel for the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. This is the most important Supreme Court election law case in a generation. Too many courts have denied candidates their right to challenge unlawful election rules such as the outrageous act of counting ballots that arrive AFTER Election Day. We will keep you informed of all the developments in this case. Our September brief [] to the High Court states: Illinois counts mail-in ballots received up to two weeks after Election Day. Petitioners, candidates for federal office, claim that under controlling federal law that is two weeks too long. As a result, Illinois is counting unlawful ballots and producing inaccurate vote tallies, while simultaneously hurting petitioners’ prospects at the ballot box and injuring their pocketbooks. We submit that the Seventh Circuit’s decision is wrong and dangerous: It is wrong because candidates have standing to challenge the rules that govern their elections, especially when their merits theory (which must be credited for standing purposes) is that the challenged rule produces an inaccurate final tally. At a minimum, the candidate has standing when (as here) he plausibly alleges that the challenged rule will harm his electoral prospects and reduce his bank balance because he needs to pay campaign staff an extra two weeks. And the decision is dangerous because it forces judges to play political prognosticators, skews standing rules to favor certain kinds of candidates, and funnels election disputes to the worst possible context—namely, after the election where judges are asked to declare political winners. This Court should reverse. We state that Bost has standing to challenge the Illinois law: At the very least, Congressman Bost has standing to challenge the Illinois ballot-receipt deadline here, as a host of diverse amici confirm. Congressman Bost plausibly alleged a substantial risk that counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day will harm his electoral prospects both by risking electoral defeat and reducing his margin of victory. The plausibility of those allegations was amply reinforced by the Illinois Democratic Party’s attempted intervention and voting and litigation patterns nationwide. And he has also plausibly alleged a classic pocketbook injury because he expended additional campaign funds as a direct result of the state’s extended deadline for receiving mail-in ballots. Here too, the notion that an election artificially extended a fortnight costs more than one that ends on Election Day hardly strains credulity. The state’s contrary arguments lack merit. In our previous Supreme Court brief [], we stated: Federal law sets the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November as the federal Election Day. * Candidates have an obvious interest in the lawfulness and fairness of the rules that govern the elections into which they pour their time and resources. They also have an obvious interest “in ensuring that the final vote tally accurately reflects the legally valid votes cast.” Candidates pour enormous resources into running for election and have an obvious interest in the rules that dictate how long their races will last and how the ballots will be counted. They also have a distinct interest “in ensuring that the final vote tally accurately reflects the legally valid votes cast.” We are a national leader [] in voting integrity and voting rights. As part of our work, we have assembled a team of highly experienced voting rights attorneys. Robert Popper, a Judicial Watch senior attorney, leads our election law program. Popper was previously in the Voting Section of the Civil Rights Division of the Justice Department, where he managed voting rights investigations, litigations, consent decrees, and settlements in dozens of states. Paul Clement, who has argued more than 100 cases before the Supreme Court, is representing Congressman Bost and the electors with us before the Supreme Court. Clement is former solicitor general under President George W. Bush from 2005-2008 and is widely regarded as among the top Supreme Court litigators in the country. T. Russell Nobile, a Judicial Watch senior attorney, is part of Judicial Watch’s voting integrity efforts and focuses on campaign and voting issues, civil rights issues, constitutional law, official misconduct by public institutions and officials, and other issues. Eric Lee is an attorney at Judicial Watch, where he focuses on enforcing federal and state laws that promote transparency and integrity in the electoral process. Eric graduated with his B.A. from St. Mary’s College of Maryland and received his J.D. from the University of Maryland School of Law. He is licensed to practice in California, Maryland, the District of Columbia, and in federal courts in Illinois and Colorado. We recently filed a brief [] to the U.S. Supreme Court on behalf of the Libertarian Party of Mississippi, opposing the State of Mississippi’s attempt to overturn the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit’s decision, which struck down a law allowing ballots received after Election Day to be counted. Federal courts in Oregon [], California and Illinois [] recently ruled that our lawsuits against those states may proceed to force them to clean their voter rolls. We announced [] in May that our work led to the removal of more than five million ineligible names from voter rolls nationwide. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES ODNI FOR RECORDS ON VOTING MACHINE VULNERABILITIES The Trump administration knows electronic voting machines are vulnerable, and we think the American people deserve transparency on this critically important matter. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the Office of the Director of National Intelligence for records on which Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard based a discussion of the vulnerabilities of electronic voting machines in an April White House cabinet meeting (Judicial Watch Inc. v. Office of the Director of National Intelligence [ (No. 1:25-cv-03526)). In March 2025, President Trump issued an executive order [] that included a directive to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to review the security of electronic voting systems. In an April 2025 White House Cabinet meeting Gabbard indicated [] that voting machines are susceptible to hacking and capable of changing votes. We sued after the Office of the Director for National Intelligence failed to respond to an April 11, 2025, FOIA request for: Any records about statements made by Director Gabbard during a cabinet meeting with President Trump in which she stated that: “We have evidence of how these electronic voting systems have been vulnerable to hackers for a very long time and vulnerable to exploitation to manipulate the results of the votes being cast...” All reports, evidence, assessments, memoranda, and/or briefings prepared by, for, or presented to the ODNI [Office of the Director of National Intelligence] (including the National Intelligence Council or any Intelligence Community component) that evaluate the security, integrity, or vulnerabilities of electronic voting systems in the United States, particularly any documents referenced or relied upon by Director Gabbard in making her statements as described above. Communications of Director Gabbard and ODNI [Office of the Director of National Intelligence] personnel or between Director Gabbard (or her designated representative) and the Executive Office of the President, the Department of Homeland Security, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation, Central Intelligence Agency, Department of Defense relating to the content or preparation of Director Gabbard's statements. We continue to fight for American voters and their right to know how elections are being carried out, which includes evidence of vulnerabilities in electronic voting systems. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES DC FOR RECORDS ON ALLEGED CRIME DATA MANIPULATION How bad is crime in your nation’s capital? We’re not entirely sure. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the District of Columbia for records related to allegations of crime data manipulation by the Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) (Judicial Watch Inc. v. District of Columbia [] (No. 2025-CAB-006701)). It was recently reported [] that DC police officers are cooperating with the U.S. Department of Justice in an investigation into whistleblower reports of manipulated crime data. The lawsuit follows DC’s failure to respond to an August 14, 2025, FOIA request for: Complaints or communications from the Fraternal Order of Police (FOP), Chairman Greggory Pemberton, or union representatives alleging MPD [Metropolitan Police Department] supervisors falsified or downgraded crime data (e.g., classifying shootings as “felony assaults” or carjackings as lesser offenses). Internal audits, reviews, or quality control assessments of crime reporting practices in the 3rd District or department-wide, including comparisons of raw incident reports to finalized Uniform Crime Reporting data. Records of past allegations from 2019-2020, including whistleblower complaints about misclassifying violent crimes (e.g., the August 2019 face-slashing or December 2019 knife-to-neck incidents reported as “simple assault”). Policies, guidelines, training materials, or directives on crime classification and reporting, including updates since 2019 on violent crime definitions (e.g., distinguishing “assault with a dangerous weapon” from “simple assault”). Communications among MPD [Metropolitan Police Department] personnel (e.g., supervisors, commanders, or data analysts) discussing adjustments to crime statistics to reflect lower violent crime rates In August, President Trump issued an executive order [], “Restoring Law and Order in the District of Columbia,” which refers to the “epidemic of crime in our Nation’s capital” and authorized the Secretary of Defense to mobilize the DC National Guard. The House Oversight Committee announced [] in August that it was launching an investigation into allegations of manipulated and inaccurate crime statistics by DC Metropolitan Police Department leadership. Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer (R-KY) stated. [I]n May, MPD [Metropolitan Police Department] placed 3rd District Commander Michael Pulliam on administrative leave following allegations that he altered crime reports. Unfortunately, this practice does not appear to be isolated, nor is it a recent development. MPD [Metropolitan Police Department] recently entered into a settlement agreement related to allegations that senior MPD [Metropolitan Police Department] officials were engaged in falsifying crime statistics to artificially lower reported crime rates. People who live in, work in, and visit Washington, DC, have the right to real transparency about crime in the nation’s capital. OKLAHOMA NABS 125 ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKERS WITH COMMERCIAL LICENSES The Trump administration is cleaning up highway safety after the careless Biden years, helping to restore law and order on our roadways. Our Corruption Chronicles blog reports [] on one state that is helping. Weeks after a criminal illegal alien with a Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) killed three people while recklessly driving a big rig on a Florida highway, officials in Oklahoma have apprehended over 125 illegal immigrants with a CDL they did not qualify for, including one listing “No Name Given” on the card. This is a widespread problem caused by state driver licensing agencies that fail to ensure truckers have proper training or legal status in the United States before issuing the special commercial licenses. Adding to the problem, many Mexican truck drivers that consistently deliver loads north of the border do not speak English and cannot read American highway signs, endangering public safety across the country. Nearly 6 million trucks crossed from Mexico into the U.S. last year, according to government figures [], and though federal regulations require drivers to sufficiently read and speak English and understand highway traffic signs the Obama administration relaxed the English proficiency rules in 2016 and directed inspectors not to penalize truckers. Sanctuary states have contributed significantly to the crisis by allowing illegal immigrants to obtain licenses to operate commercial vehicles. The illegal alien from India who killed three people with his 18-wheeler in mid-August had a valid commercial driver’s license from California, a renowned sanctuary state. His name is Harjinder Singh [], and he tried to make an illegal U-turn on a busy southeastern Florida highway in his enormous tractor trailer, suddenly blocking all oncoming lanes and causing a brutal accident that instantly killed three innocent people. Federal authorities say video from inside the truck shows the exact moment Singh decided to break U.S. highway laws as he turned his big rig into traffic. “His face shows no shock or remorse for his actions or the lives he destroyed,” a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) statement says. The illegal immigrant, who is 28 years old, was charged with three counts of vehicular homicide and recently entered a not guilty plea, according to a local news report [] that also says Singh first got his commercial driver’s license in Washington state before California. There could be untold numbers of truckers like Singh driving big rigs on highways across America. # **It 's David Shuster's Week-End Video Round Up!**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/78e56b7f-237f-4a05-93bc-b438529af964?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In this episode of his killer end-of-the-week wrap ups, [David Shuster](https://open.substack.com/users/16891317-david-shuster?utm_source=mentions) cuts through the chaos with precision and punch, unpacking a week that exposed MAGA leadership has become more hollow than that space in Mike Johnson's head where he stores day dreams of Trump.
And so the Trump machine edges ever closer to collapse.
The first headline moment lands squarely on the aforementioned, and mocked, Speaker Johnson. His "district work period" stunt effectively shuttered the House and delayed the swearing-in of Democrat Adelita Grijalva.
[That single move blocked the critical 218th signature needed to force a vote on the long-simmering Trump-Epstein files](https://substack.com/redirect/cbd79748-6b46-4950-af73-185e115116a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Shuster doesn't miss the irony: Johnson blames government dysfunction, while literally _running away_ _from doing his job_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bf333807-af8f-41d4-b21d-519723a85d80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The second key segment zeroes in on Democratic [Rep. Eric Swalwell's bombshell statement](https://substack.com/redirect/12bd67e0-8cc2-4b76-b401-f3ee78eb1d5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that "it's coming to an end."
According to Swalwell, even House Republicans are whispering that Trump's support is fading faster than J.D. Vance's public profile. And the rumored Epstein evidence could be the final blow.
The story took an even darker twist when Attorney General Merrick Garland refused to deny that the FBI possesses lewd photos of Trump with young women. Shuster calls it what it is: "a political earthquake waiting to happen."

Finally, the show pivots to the theater of the absurd: Trump declaring--because as this dunderhead once said, "I'm like, really smart"--t[hat drug prices would be reduced by "500%."](https://substack.com/redirect/0d2a39c9-a436-4030-bb0b-da266153e9ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Which, as Shuster deadpans, "would mean Big Pharma starts paying patients."
From there, we're treated to [a delusional rant about Portland "burning to the ground,"](https://substack.com/redirect/b08213b4-99db-4f55-935f-2c8dde1947f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a claim instantly contradicted by on-the-ground footage, and Kristi Noem's own ill-fated "inspection." That turned up only a protester in a chicken suit.
Meanwhile, Stephen Miller short-circuits on live TV, [while trying to justify illegal troop deployments under Title 10](https://substack.com/redirect/6a7aaa62-085f-40c2-8245-07a611e02275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a scene Shuster gleefully describes as "the broadcast Gods striking back."
Topping it all off, the _AI Clip of the Week_ drives the satire home, underlining just how grotesque and absurd the MAGA movement has become, when filtered through its own soundbites.
Shuster signs off the only way Blue Amp Media knows how--sharp, irreverent, and defiantly hopeful: _Keep laughing, keep singing, and stay strong._
